body:
📊 *weekly triage digest* — 2026-07-17 → 2026-07-24

⚠ *Window note:* the routine was dark for 6 of these 7 days (2026-07-17 → 2026-07-22, zero poll-cycles in the incident log) — the tail of the already-diagnosed 8-day laptop-hibernation gap (2026-07-15 17:08Z → 2026-07-23 20:11Z). It resumed with one large backlog catch-up (45 groups) plus two quiet cycles, all on 2026-07-23. Every number below is real, but it's the shape of a single burst-day, not 7 days of organic cadence — treat week-over-week deltas as not meaningful this cycle.

*Volume:* 48 alerts triaged · 27 posted · 4 suppressed to digest (+ 17 false-alarm self-DM confirmations, counted separately — no post, no digest entry)

*Top recurrences this week*
| occ | entry | fix_status |
|-----|-------|------------|
| 2 | ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring | investigating |
| 1 each | 24 other KB entries (ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout, ki-2026-07-03-method-ui-grid-dropdown-performance-test-nodata, ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap, +21 more) | mixed |

*New this week:* none (no KB entries with first_seen in this window)
*Aging:* oldest unchanged fix_status — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout` still `chronic-residual-post-rollback-2026-06-05` (48d unchanged, 580 occurrences all-time, #1 by volume). Broader aging audit is limited — the KB doesn't track a status-change timestamp separately from the status string itself.
*Concentration:* top 3 = 4 of this week's 26 KIR occurrences (~15%) — unusually flat vs the standing ~64% top-3-of-all-time figure, because the catch-up burst logged most chronic entries exactly once instead of at their normal hourly cadence. Not a real de-concentration trend.
*Suppression ratio:* 4/48 (~8%) suppressed to digest this week — unusually low. The single mega-cycle's 24h KIR window had expired for almost every chronic entry simultaneously (last touched before the gap), so nearly everything resurfaced as a post instead of being suppressed.

One thing worth doing next week: confirm the hibernation-gap fix (watchdog / wake scheduling) actually holds — this is the second consecutive digest window disrupted by it.
